description: Harvested reproducers: concrete HGVS rows that carry a behavioural claim from an issue, a PR description or a campaign note, and that until now nothing running in CI could fail on. Every row was re-measured against the prepared reference and is served here from the committed slice beside this file, so the gate blocks a PR rather than skipping for want of FERRO_MANIFEST. Rows are of three kinds: pinned (expected is a string ferro must still produce), confluent (rows sharing confluence_class must produce one string, and where the governing ruling is open no string is pinned), and red (defect is set — the row reproduces a live defect, its expected records today's wrong answer, and the #[ignore]d guard naming the issue fails until it is fixed).

citation.quote: **more than one nucleotide** replacing the original sequence is the reverse complement of the original sequence

cases.note: The flagship row of this corpus. c.76_83 reads AATGCACA and its reverse complement is TGTGCATT, so the whole block IS an inversion by definition. The two spellings that compete with it coincide at the four interior columns 78-81 (both read TGCA), which is why the block can also be spelled as two delins. This is the one row where the exact string is pinned: the ruling inversion-vs-two-delins-76-83 is DECIDED, and #1535 implemented it. Pinning it here is the only instrument that can catch a regression -- #1535 itself reported `Representation-Change: 0 rows move over 5,761,302 real expressions`, not because the fix was inert but because no generator in the tree can build a block whose reverse complement coincides with its reference at the interior columns. IT IS ALSO THE CONTROL FOR #1541: this class competes with delins and must prefer inv, while the NM_000500.9:c.710_713 class competes with substitutions and must prefer the split. Holding both is what stops the rule being written as 'always prefer the split' -- or 'always prefer inv'.

citation.quote: **and which is not** a substitution or inversion

cases.note: The two-member delins spelling of the same block, converging on the inv. inversion.md:5 and delins.md:5 are a definitional-exclusion pair, not a ranking: a change that IS the reverse complement of its reference is an inversion, and delins is defined as what is left over once substitution and inversion are excluded. So no prioritisation argument is needed to decide this row. Sequence equivalence was verified from raw FASTA, transcript against genome-via-cdot with reverse complement for this minus-strand transcript.

citation.quote: two variants separated by one nucleotide, together affecting one amino acid, should be described as a "delins"

cases.note: c.1_3 reads ATG -- the initiation codon -- and both changes land in it, separated by the unchanged c.2. general.md:35 is exactly on point, so the pair must converge. No string is pinned: which of the two legal spellings ships is a representation choice (canonical-form-choice-when-both-legal is undecided), and asserting agreement is the correctness claim the spec supports. NOTE ON THE INPUT: the widely-quoted spelling of this row is `c.[1G>T;3T>A]`, which carries WRONG reference bases on BOTH members -- c.1 is A and c.3 is G. It must never be used as an input here; #1543 records that ferro currently accepts it in strict mode because reference validation is bypassed for cis members close enough to be merged.

citation.quote: the most 3' position possible of the reference sequence is arbitrarily assigned to have been changed

cases.note: A plain 3'rule shift over a homopolymer, and nothing running per-PR asserted its repair target. In the enumeration fixture the row is `requires-reference` and in the normalization fixture it is `false-acceptance`, and BOTH committed guards skip those statuses -- so the spec's own rule had a repair target that no test compared against. That is the single clearest gap this corpus closes.

A 1-nt repeat unit on a coding reference: not a multiple of 3, so repeat notation is unavailable (:21) and the spec prints the description to use instead (:22). Sequence-dependent -- the tract has to be read -- so it cannot fire in the MockProvider-backed spec fixture, where it sits as a skipped status.

citation.quote: two variants separated by one or more nucleotides should be described individually and **not** as a "delins"

cases.note: MOVED 2026-08-10 by `two_gap_deletion_alignment`, from the spanning `g.45891619_45891622delinsC` to the two-member split. NOT a re-bless of a spec-correctness claim: this row was a STABILITY PIN and stability is a tiebreaker, not a veto — the project bar is confluence plus disclosure. The two members are separated by ONE unchanged nucleotide (g.45891620), so the decided ruling `delins-merge-vs-individual-gap-two-or-more` does not reach it: that ruling is scoped by its own terms to a gap of two or more, and the row is `g.`, where `general.md:35`'s codon exception cannot apply either. What does reach it is `general.md:34` ("two variants separated by one or more nucleotides should be described individually and **not** as a 'delins'"), which asks for exactly this split. The earlier note said the governing ruling was open; it was decided 2026-08-07, and scoped away from this row. The pin now records the split as the form `general.md:34` states, and the citation moves with it.

citation.quote: **The "delins" format is recommended**: it is simpler and prevents software tools making incorrect predictions

cases.note: The spec's own worked non-confluent pair, held on the spanning-delins side. Note carefully what :47 does and does not say: it RECOMMENDS the delins format, it does not prohibit the split that :46 calls the alternative description. So this is a stability pin backed by a recommendation, not a rule -- and the pair itself is the subject of the open ruling delins-merge-vs-individual-gap-two-or-more.

citation.quote: the variant is described as `LRG_199t1:c.3921dup`

cases.note: PRESERVATION ONLY. The exon/exon-junction carve-out from the 3'rule (the rule itself is background/numbering.md:22-24). What is pinned is that this row does not move. It is the near side of the clamp, and it stays put under the now-DECIDED ruling exon-junction-dup-converge-from-the-far-side as well: that ruling moves the SIBLING c.3922dup onto this row's answer (#1621), it does not move this one. Cited at :25-26 because that is where the LRG_199t1 spelling of the worked example lives; :58 states the same example as NC_000023.11(NM_004006.2) and is the wrong citation for this row.

citation.quote: the variant is described as `LRG_199t1:c.3921dup`

cases.note: PRE-FIX BEHAVIOUR, NOT PRESERVATION-BY-DESIGN. The ruling `exon-junction-dup-converge-from-the-far-side` is now DECIDED: CONVERGE — c.3922dup must normalize to c.3921dup, because the 3'rule's exon-junction clamp binds from both sides. This row pins where ferro leaves it TODAY; when #1621 lands, `expected` becomes `LRG_199t1:c.3921dup`.

citation.quote: downstream of the frameshift are not described unless they change the amino acid sequence or length of the shifted reading frame

cases.note: STABILITY PIN PLUS A CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS. A prior audit suspected a denotation bug here and cited delins.md:19. It is not a denotation bug: c.242..249 reads CAAGGGTA, and both the input and ferro's output yield AAAGGTT -- verified sequence-equivalent. So this is a representation question, not a correctness one. The clause that actually bears on it is protein/frameshift.md:24, since the input's first member is a frame-shifting deletion and what follows it downstream is what the two spellings disagree about. Whether ferro's form is the right representation has NOT been adjudicated, so this row asserts stability only and must not be read as endorsement. #1835 PARTITION DEFAULT FLIP: re-pinned from `NM_006420.3:c.[242del;245G>A;249A>T]` to the authored spelling, which is what the re-derivation happens to yield here — NOT the input being preserved. `derivation-may-not-be-bounded-by-the-inputs-spelling` (decided) removed the input-relative bound; that the derived form coincides with the input on this row is a property of the sequence. The representation question the note above records is still unadjudicated, and this row still asserts stability only.

citation.quote: the preferred description is: (1) substitution, (2) deletion, (3) inversion, (4) duplication, (5) insertion

cases.note: #1541's class, and this spelling is the form the class converges on today. c.710_713 reads TCGT and its reverse complement is ACGA; the interior CG is self-complementary, so the inversion changes only the flanks -- which is exactly what these two substitutions write. VERIFIED EQUIVALENT, and the reference bases at 710 and 713 genuinely are T. NO LONGER A LIVE REPRODUCER: the class did not converge while Normalizer::is_splittable_single_member matched only HV::Genome/HV::Mt, so a lone c. member never reached the sequence-first pass; PR #1484 widened that gate to c./n./r. and merged 2026-08-08, and all three spellings now converge. The `defect` was dropped and the guard case_harvest::the_four_mer_inversion_pair_converges un-ignored in the same change, as the census assertion requires. THE FORM IS STILL NOT ADJUDICATED, WHICH IS WHY THIS ROW PINS NO OUTPUT. #1541 asked for a ruling on which form governs and then convergence on it; convergence arrived as a side effect and no ruling was made, so the issue stays open. This note used to say the target was decided by general.md:56 ranking substitution (1) above inversion (3). THAT GROUNDING IS WITHDRAWN: the decided record adjudication-precedence-order, entry E1, says :56 ranks single-variant type labels for one span and 'cannot settle a merge-versus-split question at all', which is exactly what this class is. The sibling decided record inversion-vs-two-delins-76-83 reads :56 the other way; the two are in tension and that is the operator's call. #1541's 2026-08-12 status also records this locus as a live member of the #1703 family (GTTAA -> TTAAC is the identical shape at 5 nt) and that whichever way that is ruled, this row moves with it. The exact form is held only as a stability tripwire in the guard, on background/basics.md:38.

citation.quote: **and which is not** a substitution or inversion

cases.note: #1541's class, the delins spelling -- the third member, and the one that makes it as strong as the NM_004006.2 class. The payload ACGA is exactly revcomp(TCGT), so delins.md:5 excludes the delins typing outright and the row must be re-typed. CORRECTION TO AN OLDER MEASUREMENT, KEPT BECAUSE IT WAS REPORTED WRONG ONCE: this row was reported as a fixed point on main; it was not -- it normalized to c.710_713inv, so the class split 2-versus-1 rather than three ways. Since PR #1484 merged (2026-08-08) all three spellings converge on c.[710T>A;713T>A]. No output is pinned here, and the class carries no `defect` any more: it no longer reproduces non-convergence, while #1541 stays open because the form was never ruled on. See the two-substitution row.

defect.summary: a dup-shaped split still emits members at separation 0 (delins.md:16), surviving #1537

cases.note: LIVE DEFECT #1542. The reference span reads CTGA and the output is sequence-equivalent to the input. Under sep = next.start - prev.end - 1 the members at 80110044 and 80110045 are at separation 0, which delins.md:16 forbids. #1537 fixed three sibling rows of this family and did not reach this one because of the dup shape. THE SEPARATION READING IS ITSELF PART OF THE OPEN QUESTION: the adjacency depends on treating a dup as occupying the position it duplicates. Read as zero-width -- an interbase reading -- the pair is not adjacent and this row is not a violation at all. The expected string above records today's output so movement is still detected; it is not an endorsement. This is the ONLY row exempted from the corpus-wide separation-0 check, and it is exempt because it is the reproducer for it. #1835 PARTITION DEFAULT FLIP: re-pinned from `NC_000017.11:g.[80110044C>G;80110045dup;80110047A>G]`. THE OUTPUT NO LONGER PUTS TWO MEMBERS AT SEPARATION 0 — `80110044delinsGT` and `80110047A>G` are two unchanged bases apart. DO NOT READ THAT AS #1542 BEING FIXED. The row has stopped REACHING the defect because the whole block is now re-partitioned from the resulting sequence and no `dup`-shaped split is produced at all; the open question the note above states — how a `dup`'s extent is read for the purpose of `sep = next.start - prev.end - 1` — is untouched, and the code path that produced the touching pair is still there for any input that still reaches it. The `defect` field, this row's place in the red set and the `#[ignore]` on `the_dup_shaped_split_does_not_touch` are therefore all left as they are. Closing #1542 needs the ruling, not this re-pin.
